items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: When I was playing with him... And Eddie Yank on trombone. Yank Johnson on trombone.

ctx.x: Oh. Who were the three tracks with the Arnold one? I couldn't get that.

That's the Arnold man. When I was playing with him. Mm-hmm. When I was playing with him, there were Maurice, Manuel Perez, and that sometime Rick. Mm-hmm. And sometime another trumpet player. Uh-huh. But Maurice and Manuel was the main trumpet players. Mm-hmm. And, uh, Eddie Yank on trombone. Yank Johnson on trombone. And Piku played with us. Uh-huh. And sometime Eddie Sherry playing that. Had old man Tatt baritone. Mm-hmm. And who else was playing trombone with the Ancret to trombone? Well, I'm afraid. I never…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I remember who the trombones were. Yank Johnson, and we used a guy called Gaia... He played trombone in our brass band a long time.

ctx.x: How many were in that band about? Ten. Ten. Ten. How many trumpets? Do you remember? Three. Three?

Emanuel Perez, Maurice Duran, and sometimes Ricard. But I can't remember the other regular member. No, but Ricard. I remember who the trombones were. Yank Johnson, and we used a guy called Gaia. You know the guy who used to play banjo? Butler rap. Yeah, butler rap. That's right. He played trombone. I didn't know that. Yeah, he played trombone in our brass band a long time.

They had alto horns or saxes or anything? Yeah, we had real alto. Old man Bob Rand. Oh yes. He played, and who baritone played? Tats Daddy. Oh yes, Alexander. Yeah, old man Alexander. Adolph, his name is Adolph.
